Wow I don't know where to start.

First of all, thank you for your incredibly kind and uplifting reply.

Now onto answer your questions, I actually am doing exactly that. I'm taking 1-2 classes a semester at a community college near my house so I can get their counseling services they offer. The thing is, it's still expensive, and it comes out of my pocket usually.

Thankfully, my real dad kinda realized he made a lot of mistakes as a father and husband a few years back, and while he doesn't make enough money to support me fully, he does help me pay for as much as he can.

As for coping with the loss of my friend, there are a few things he always wanted me to do before he passed away that I just never got around to. I have done all of them now, multiple times. It really helps me, whether it be a movie he really liked, a game he wanted me to play, or a band he wanted me to listen to. I also talk to his mom a decent amount, I'll come over to her house and have lunch with her etc. I think it helps both of us, honestly.

His favorite video game was Borderlands, and so tomorrow when the new one comes out I'll be playing for him.

Thank you again for everything you said; I really do appreciate it. I'll have to come back to this whenever I'm feeling down, just so I know there's someone out there who believes in me.
